llm.summary: The package is internally consistent with an LMail operations toolset, but it includes scripts that access system paths and perform file writes/copies (including defaults that target /root and /opt), plus admin-capable endpoints — these behaviors warrant caution before installing or running untrusted scripts.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included scripts: registration, PoW solving, login/verify, inbox polling, send/ack, and admin audit/override. Required binaries (python3, curl) and required config (lmail.base_url) align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the shipped scripts which read/write credentials, poll inboxes, and call admin endpoints. Some shipped helper scripts (sync_docs_check.sh, install_for_openclaw.sh, publish_clawhub.sh) reference or operate on host filesystem locations (/opt/lmail, /root/clawd/skills) and external tooling (clawhub/npx). Those actions go beyond simple API calls and can touch system-wide files if executed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), but the package contains many executable scripts. The included install_for_openclaw.sh and publish_clawhub.sh copy files and invoke external CLIs (clawhub / npx). There is no remote download, so code is local, but running these scripts can write into system locations.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Metadata declares no secrets and only a config key (lmail.base_url), which matches the service-focused purpose. However scripts expect/produce credential material (LMAIL_CREDENTIALS_FILE / .lmail-credentials.json) and accept admin-token/admin-api-key arguments—powerful credentials not enforced in frontmatter. The package will persist apiKey/token to disk (with chmod 0600), which is reasonable for an ops tool but requires the user to supply sensitive credentials. No unrelated external credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good), but some scripts default to copying into /root/clawd/skills and reading /opt/lmail paths; executing them as-is may require elevated privileges and will modify host state. The skill also persists credentials to files in the working filesystem. Autonomy is enabled by default (disable-model-invocation:false), which increases blast radius if automated invocation is combined with privileged host operations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to be a legitimate LMail operations toolkit, but treat it as powerful: it persists API keys/tokens to disk, calls admin endpoints, and includes scripts that read/write system paths (/opt/lmail, default install target /root/clawd/skills) or invoke external CLIs (npx/clawhub). Before installing or executing: review the scripts line-by-line, do not run install/publish scripts as root unless you intend to change system directories, confirm the lmail.base_url you will target (do not use the example host unless you trust it), store credentials in a secure location and use least-privilege admin tokens, and prefer running initially in an isolated environment (container / VM) to observe behavior. If you want a lower-risk test, run non-destructive scripts (preflight_check.sh, smoke test with --register omitted, or solve_pow.py locally) and avoid admin_* and install_* scripts until comfortable.
